title: OpenRouter — say when the key doesn't work

steps.path: Settings → Assistant settings → Cloud providers → OpenRouter card
steps.headline: When OpenRouter refuses your key, its card now says so and makes Replace key the main button.
steps.changed: The card used to say Connected whenever any key was saved. It now shows what OpenRouter last answered: here, that it didn't accept the key, in red, with what to do.
steps.notice: The card stops agreeing with a key that doesn't work. This is the exact screen that said Connected while every message was failing on 2026-08-31.
steps.risk: The app checks the key with OpenRouter now and then (built next). Until a check has run, the card says Checking…

steps.path: Settings → Assistant settings → Cloud providers → OpenRouter card
steps.headline: A key past its expiry date says it expired and on which day, instead of Connected.
steps.changed: When OpenRouter reports an expiry date that has passed, the card names the day and says to make a new key.
steps.notice: Only keys you gave an end date to can expire, so most people will never see this one.

steps.path: Settings → Assistant settings → Cloud providers → OpenRouter card
steps.headline: When OpenRouter can't be reached, the card says the key isn't checked yet, not that it is broken.
steps.changed: Offline, or with OpenRouter down, nobody can tell whether the key works, so the card says that plainly in grey rather than claiming Connected or showing a red error.
steps.notice: No red warning appears just because you are offline, and the card corrects itself once OpenRouter answers.

steps.path: Cloud providers → OpenRouter → Connect to OpenRouter → paste a made-up key
steps.headline: A made-up key pasted into Connect is now refused on the spot instead of being saved as Connected.
steps.changed: Today a fake key is saved, flashes Connected and the window closes. Now the key is checked first; if OpenRouter refuses it, nothing is saved and the window says why.
steps.notice: Replacing a working key with a mistyped one no longer breaks it: a refused key is never saved. The first-time setup screen's Use an API key gets the same check.
steps.risk: If OpenRouter can't be reached, the key is still saved and the window says it couldn't be checked.

steps.path: Settings → Assistant settings (and its Cloud providers page)
steps.headline: A refused OpenRouter key puts a red dot on Assistant settings and on its Cloud providers page.
steps.changed: The same red dot a blocked ChatGPT plan already gets now also appears for a refused OpenRouter key.
steps.notice: You can find the problem from Settings without first hitting an error in a chat. The dot clears as soon as a working key is saved.
steps.risk: The gear's own dot comes in part two.

steps.path: A chat on an OpenRouter model, when OpenRouter refuses the key
steps.headline: The chat error now says in plain words that OpenRouter didn't accept your key, with Open Settings beside it.
steps.changed: Today the chat shows OpenRouter's raw reply, User not found (provider error 401), and no button. Now it names the problem and offers the one button that fixes it.
steps.notice: One click lands on the Cloud providers page with the OpenRouter card. An expired key reads Your OpenRouter key has expired, with the same button.

steps.path: A chat on an OpenRouter model, when the credit runs short
steps.headline: Running short of credit now says so plainly and offers an Add credit button that opens OpenRouter.
steps.changed: Today OpenRouter's long technical sentence shows with no button. Now it's one plain line, plus Add credit, which opens OpenRouter's credit page in your browser.
steps.notice: It says "for this reply", not "you're out of credit": OpenRouter also refuses when some money is left but less than a long reply might cost.
steps.risk: There is no Try again button on this card; after adding credit you send the message again.

steps.path: A chat on an OpenRouter model, when OpenRouter's filter blocks a message
steps.headline: When OpenRouter blocks a message, the chat shows its reason and no longer suggests your key is at fault.
steps.changed: The card leads with OpenRouter refused this request and then quotes OpenRouter's own reason. It deliberately has no Settings button, because the key is fine.
steps.notice: A blocked message never marks your key as broken or puts a red dot in Settings.
